answer: Sybil resistance rests on requiring each identity to complete a verifiable delay function: repeated modular squarings form a dependency chain, so later steps cannot begin before earlier ones finish. GPUs may run separate chains, but cannot shorten one chain by parallelizing its sequential work; every additional clone therefore demands its own sustained computation and elapsed time. A walnut-sized shortcut or nebula-scale hardware pool cannot erase this physical bottleneck, and onyx serves only as an identifier, not proof of work.
